response.agreement_with_paper: Independent linear-wave and sediment-transport estimates confirm non-breaking conditions and strong mobility (theta/theta_c=3.67). The Sumer-Fredsøe equilibrium gives S_eq/D=0.247, consistent with the CFD curve trending upward; fitting a single time-scale T*=1054 s reproduces Fig. 10(b) within RMS ~0.010 in S/D across 200–1200 s. The literature time-scale (379 s) is ~3× faster than the paper’s approach but within known scatter.
gaps: No rerun of the paper’s 3D RANS k–epsilon + VOF CFD or sediment modules
Time evolution matched via a fitted relaxation time (T*), not fully predicted from first principles
No validation of suspended-load transport, sand-slide, or turbulence/VOF parameter choices
No direct digitized comparison to Sumer et al. (1992) raw experimental time series; only figure-level matching
No sensitivity analysis to roughness, theta_c, or friction-factor choice
Sections on breaking-wave beach evolution and breaking-wave pile scour (§6.2, §6.3) not attempted
response.recommendation: Classify as PARTIAL: the §6.1 non-breaking pile-scour trend and magnitude are independently supported, but the CFD engine and breaking-wave cases were not reproduced and the time-scale required fitting.
